To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) XGBoost is the best algorithm for maize yield forecasting, and (2) the prediction can be improved by using hundreds of features derived from a variety of data sources.

1) the XGBoost algorithm is the best choice among six algorithms tested; 2) a large number of environmental variables (i.e., 300+ features) is necessary for accurate crop yield forecasting; 3) the compositing interval of time series data has little impact on the prediction accuracy; and 4) the early-season yield forecasting is possible, with a prediction error of 0.4 t/ha at the national scale.

1) a comprehensive composite of environmental variables is needed to achieve reasonable yield prediction accuracy; 2) XGBoost outperforms other machine learning algorithms, while LSTM and CNN do not improve the prediction accuracy; 3) the compositing interval of time series variables does not have significant effect on the prediction; and 4) the prediction accuracy of the best model is comparable to that of the USDA WADSE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods to improve yield prediction and to understand how crop yield responds to environmental variables.
developing and testing the best algorithm for crop yield prediction, and assessing the effects of environmental variables on the prediction accuracy.
the development of a comprehensive crop yield prediction system that can be useful for a range of users, from farmers and agribusiness to policy makers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of a large set of features (i.e. hundreds of features) and a sophisticated machine learning algorithm (i.e., XGBoost) is the most effective approach for crop yield prediction.
the best prediction model should be a hybrid model that combines a large set of environmental variables and a state-of-the-art algorithm.

1) the XGBoost algorithm is the best choice in terms of both accuracy and stability; 2) a large composite of environmental information is needed for accurate yield prediction; 3) the compositing intervals of the environmental information have no significant effects on the accuracy; and 4) the prediction can be achieved as early as June, four months prior to the harvest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
crop yield forecasting can benefit from more advanced algorithms and an extensive set information, such as canopy, stress, soil, and phenology.
the prediction of maize yield at county level is feasible and can be improved with more advanced algorithms and more environmental inputs.
a large composite of environmental information and a sophisticated algorithm are both essential for accurate crop yield prediction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of algorithm is critical to the prediction accuracy and the choice of input variables is also critical to the stability of predictions.
the use of a large number of environmental variables and the application of advanced machine learning algorithms can significantly improve the accuracy of yield predictions.
crop yield prediction is a challenging task and the prediction accuracy depends on both the availability of environmental data and the choice of machine learning algorithm.
